findings.quote: Only a mutation in the cells that make gametes can pass to offspring.
findings.problem: False absolute. In asexual reproduction a mutation passes to offspring with no gametes: a mutation in a bacterium passes to its daughter cells by binary fission, and a somatic mutation in a plant passes on through cuttings or grafts (for example bud sports). Bacterial antibiotic resistance from mutation is a standard natural selection item, and this rule would lead a student to deny that the mutation is inherited. The sentence holds only for sexually reproducing animals with a separate germ line, and the lesson states no such condition.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); B01; standard reference: OpenStax Biology 2e, 22.2 (prokaryotes reproduce by binary fission); the branch lesson characteristics-of-life teaches asexual reproduction with one parent

findings.quote: Parents pass alleles to their offspring only through gametes.
findings.problem: False absolute. In asexual reproduction (binary fission, budding, vegetative propagation) one parent passes alleles to offspring with no gametes. The same limit is missing in Example #3 step 1 ("which means variation in alleles passed through gametes") and Trap #4 ("not passed on unless they alter gamete alleles"), which define heritability as passage through gametes. A student would then misjudge heritable variation in bacteria and asexual plants, which natural selection items use.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); B01; OpenStax Biology 2e, ch. 43.1 (asexual reproduction); branch lesson characteristics-of-life line 24

findings.quote: If one is missing, it is not selection.
findings.problem: The rule makes change across generations a requirement for natural selection. That breaks at stabilizing selection, where selection favors the intermediate form and keeps the population the same (human birth weight is the textbook case). It also contradicts the lesson's own Core Concept, which says selection needs three things: variation, heritability and differential reproductive success, with no change requirement. A student would call a stabilizing selection case not selection.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); B01; OpenStax Biology 2e, 19.3 Adaptive Evolution (stabilizing selection favors the average phenotype and reduces variation); lesson line 52 to 56

findings.quote: is the pair of alleles an individual carries for a gene.
findings.problem: False as a general definition. A male carries one allele for an X-linked gene (the prerequisite genetics lesson writes such genotypes as X^CY or X^cY), and haploid organisms carry one allele per gene. Example #1 step 1 repeats the generalization ("Each individual has two copies of the gene"). The prerequisite lesson limits the two-allele rule to genes on non-sex chromosomes; this lesson drops that condition, so a student counting gene copies in a population could double-count males for an X-linked gene.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (boundary test); B01; branch lesson genetics-and-heredity lines 24 and 160 (two alleles for a gene on a non-sex chromosome; son genotype X^CY or X^cY)

findings.quote: Gene flow stops. Each group then changes through its own mutations, drift and selection.
findings.problem: This paragraph has five sentences, over the one-to-three limit. Several other paragraphs also run to four or five sentences: the nonrandom mating paragraph, the second mutation paragraph, the species paragraph, the reproductive isolation paragraph, the sympatric speciation paragraph, the adaptive radiation paragraph and the causes-of-evolution exam strategy.
findings.source: Content checklist L22a; LSG Formatting rules (paragraphs 1 to 3 short sentences)
